reasons: The 'missing' classification is supported: the cited paragraphs (Content delivery, artistic/editorial control, General Manager duties) and the rationale's survey of the rest of the Agreement (confidentiality only, Marks licence only, Section 10.2 merely disclaiming co-ownership of the relationship) show no clause allocating ownership of the Site, deliverables or customer/order data, which the IP rule expects.

The inserted Section 5.5 reaches the preferred position with a single, self-contained addition: Customer retains Content, Marks and customer/order data; HDI assigns the Site and other deliverables; HDI keeps pre-existing platform/tools subject to a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence back limited to embedded/necessary materials; express no-assignment-of-Customer-IP and no joint-ownership language.

No existing clause is being upgraded from an acceptable fallback (there is no ownership clause at all), so this is not over-flagging; deterministic checks confirm no residual assignment of Customer IP/data to the Vendor.

The comment is accurate, first-person plural, concise, states what changed and why, and offers the licence-back fallback if HDI insists on retaining its generic tools; placement of the new subsection after the end of Section 5.4 is workable.
